sections.content_markdown: Density of the salted water: $\rho = \frac{1\text{ kg} + 0.25\text{ kg}}{1200 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3} = 1.04 \times 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3$

**Question:** Density of Dead Sea water of Jordan is $1.24\text{ kg/liter}$. What is the volume of $1\text{ kg}$ water?

**Answer:** $1\text{ liter}$ is $1000\text{ cc}$ or $10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$.

Therefore, density of Dead Sea water,
$$\rho = 1.24 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{liter}} = \frac{1.24\text{ kg}}{10^{-3}\text{ m}^3} = 1.24 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$$

Therefore, volume of $1\text{ kg}$ water:
$$V = \frac{m}{\rho} = \frac{1\text{ kg}}{1.24 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}} = 0.81 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$$
or $0.81\text{ liter}$

**Example:** What is the density of the nucleus? What is the mass of $1$ tea spoonful of nucleus?

Nucleus consists of neutrons and protons. The mass of one of them is $1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$. Their approximate radius is $1.25\text{ fm} = 1.25 \times 10^{-15}\text{ m}$. Therefore, if we can calculate the density of neutron or proton, it can be considered as the density of the nucleus!

Density of nucleus, $\rho = \frac{m}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3} = \frac{1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}}{\frac{4}{3}\pi (1.25 \times 10^{-15}\text{ m})^3} = 0.204 \times 10^{18}\text{ kg/m}^3$

You need to guess how big this number is! One tea spoon contains approximately $1\text{ cc}$ materials.

Therefore, mass of $1\text{ tea spoon}$ nucleus is:
$$m = 0.204 \times 10^{18}\text{ kg/m}^3 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 = 2 \times 10^{11}\text{ kg}$$

It is roughly the collective mass of all the people of the world.
